## kb_to_source
Every normative sentence of the 30 policy documents in scope (4 hubs, 4 computation documents, 22 factor documents) and of the base/figure documents they rest on (renewal_charge_terms, renewal_grace_period, domain_refund_rules, refund_window_table, tld_price_schedule, registration_term_limits, post_expiry_stage_lengths, expiry_lifecycle_timeline, multi_domain_renewal_orders) traces to the rule, overwrite, baseline, factor ladder, base policy or variant parameters above. Derivations checked and admitted: refund-sheet tables (cap/zero rows), late-fee day table (8 → 4.00, 24 → cap), maximum-term worked months, hosting-credit "any other term → nothing" row, deposit-window edge examples, "not as it stood when the charge was billed" (= "read … on the day of the price match"). No addition of a confirmation, review, notification or step. Cross-problem operational guidance: none (each tool named only in its own hub's invocation block). Opening world state written as policy fact: none (no customer, domain, date or amount of either task appears; scored-value and id grep 0 hits).
Note (not a defect): domain_refund_rules labels clauses 1, 4, 6-part, 8, 9 "no longer in force" without scope while refund_window_table still states "a window of 0 means that charge type is never refunded"; the hubs' every-other-refund sentence (the source's replaced_by) states those rules continue for every refund other than the four price matches, so the corpus entails the source's scoped retirement.

## bijection_verdict
PASS — no omission, change of meaning or addition across the full domain of the four policies, their factors, prerequisites and retired surface.

## dependency_form
- Hop marks from the blind answer: R←A, R←B, A←C all state-derived; none pre-solved.
- Prerequisite sentences appear once each, on the blocked side (maximum_term_amount, maximum_term_extension, late_reactivation_fee); depended-on hubs (grace_period_renewal_billing, domain_care_grace/manual_*) carry no blocked-side sentence and name no waiting policy.
- No other problem's tool name in any document (each of the 8 task tools appears only in its own hub). No route, checklist, ordered multi-problem procedure, dependency table, wrong-vs-right contrast or chain example.
- The Domain Care hubs' "save the Domain Care price matches of … each set by the rule that names it" and the renewal scope sentences naming maximum-term / restore-day pricing are the source's own replaced_by carve-outs, not dependencies.
- Titles are general subjects (e.g. "Maximum-Term Extensions of Domain Registrations", "Late Reactivation Fee Tariff for Grace-Period Renewals of Domain Registrations"); none mirrors the task.
- Computation documents state the baseline; their "the amounts named as one of the … credits" and "the percentage discount that applies" are the source baseline's own wording. Factor documents state ladders as rules, name no tier a customer is on, and point at no other document.
KB-EXPLICIT: **PASS**.
